{{MedalSilver|[[EuroBasket 2022|2022 Czech Republic–Georgia–Italy–Germany]]|}} }} '''Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot''' ({{IPA|fr|timɔte luwawu kabaʁo}}; born 9 May 1995) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He was selected 24th overall pick by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the [[2016 NBA draft]]. ==Professional career== ===Olympique Antibes (2012–2015)=== Between 2012 and 2014, Luwawu-Cabarrot played a total of five games for the [[Olympique Antibes|Antibes Sharks]]. In January 2014 he signed his first pro deal with Antibes,{{Cite web |date=13 January 2014 |title=Antibes announced Winston. Luwawu-Cabarrot signed his first deal |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/110284/antibes-announced-winston-luwawu-cabarrot-signed-his-first-deal.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820171920/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/110284/antibes-announced-winston-luwawu-cabarrot-signed-his-first-deal.html |archive-date=20 August 2016 |access-date=3 July 2016 |website=Sportando.com}} and in 2014–15, he became a full squad member for the first time. In 42 games for Antibes in 2014–15, he averaged 7.1 points, 2.5 rebounds, 1.6 assists, and 1.1 steals per game. He also helped the team win the [[LNB Pro B]] [[Leaders Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/Actualites/Luwawu-cabarrot-la-pepite-d-antibes/538011|title=Luwawu-Cabarrot, la pépite d'Antibes|work=lequipe.fr|date=26 February 2015|access-date=3 July 2016|language=fr}} He originally planned to enter the [[2015 NBA draft]],{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/236476/Frances-Timothe-Luwawu-Cabarrot-Plans-Early-Entry-In-NBA-Draft|title=France's Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot Plans Early Entry In NBA Draft|work=RealGM.com|date=1 February 2015|access-date=3 July 2016}} but ultimately did not. ===Mega Leks (2015–2016)=== On 5 July 2015, Luwawu-Cabarrot signed with [[KK Mega Basket|Mega Leks]] of Serbia for the 2015–16 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/serbia/167233/mega-leks-signs-timothe-luwawu-cabarrot-and-alpha-kaba.html|title=Mega Leks signs Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot and Alpha Kaba|work=Sportando.com|date=5 July 2015|access-date=3 July 2016}} He helped the club win the [[Radivoj Korać Cup|Serbian Cup]], and at the season's end, he earned [[All-ABA League Team]] honours.{{cite web|url=http://www.aba-liga.com/news/tabid/86/id/36374/dragievi-heads-the-ideal-starting-five.aspx|title=Dragićević heads the Ideal Starting Five|work=ABA-Liga.com|date=11 March 2016|access-date=3 July 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160311185713/http://www.aba-liga.com/news/tabid/86/id/36374/dragievi-heads-the-ideal-starting-five.aspx|archive-date=11 March 2016}} In 28 [[2015–16 ABA League|ABA League]] games for Mega Leks, he averaged 14.6 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.7 steals per game. ===Philadelphia 76ers (2016–2018)=== In April 2016, Luwawu-Cabarrot declared for the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/196683/mega-leks-luwawu-zubac-kaba-jaramaz-and-zagorac-to-enter-2016-nba-draft.html|title=Mega Leks' Luwawu, Zubac, Kaba, Jaramaz and Zagorac to enter 2016 NBA Draft|work=Sportando.com|date=11 April 2016|access-date=3 July 2016}} He was subsequently selected with the 24th overall pick in the draft by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|last=Cato|first=Tim|url=https://www.sbnation.com/2016/6/23/11857188/nba-draft-2016-timothe-luwawu-cabarrot-philadelphia-76ers|title=NBA Draft 2016: 76ers select Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot at No. 24|work=SBNation.com|date=23 June 2016|access-date=3 July 2016}} On 3 July 2016, he signed his rookie scale contract with the 76ers and joined the team for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/sixers-announce-team-has-signed-2016-draft-picks-ben-simmons-and-timothe-luwawu-cabarrot|title=Sixers Announce Team Has Signed 2016 Draft Picks Ben Simmons and Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot|work=NBA.com|date=3 July 2016|access-date=3 July 2016}}{{cite web|first=Ray|last=Boyd|url=http://philadelphia.cbslocal.com/2016/07/01/ben-simmons-headlines-sixers-summer-league-roster/|title=Ben Simmons Headlines Sixers Summer League Roster|work=CBSLocal.com|date=1 July 2016|access-date=4 January 2017}} On 29 October 2016, he made his NBA debut in a 104–72 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]], recording one rebound, one assist and one steal in six minutes off the bench.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/luwawti01/gamelog/2017/|title=Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=2 February 2017}} On 1 February 2017, he made the first start of his career in place of the injured [[Robert Covington]] and scored seven points in a 113–95 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899402|title=Curry, Mejri lead Mavericks to 113-95 win over 76ers|work=ESPN.com|date=1 February 2017|access-date=2 February 2017}} On 12 March 2017, he scored a season-high 18 points in a 118–116 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900385|title=Saric, Okafor lead 76ers past Lakers 118-116|work=ESPN.com|date=12 March 2017|access-date=13 March 2017}} On 31 March 2017, he set a new season high with 19 points in a 122–105 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900523|title=LeBron, Cavs end rough March with 122-105 win over 76ers|work=ESPN.com|date=31 March 2017|access-date=2 April 2017}} Two days later, he had a 23-point effort in a 113–105 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899440|title=Raptors register ninth straight home win over 76ers, 113-105|work=ESPN.com|date=2 April 2017|access-date=2 April 2017}} On 10 April 2017, he scored a season-best 24 points in a 120–111 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900581|title=Pacers beat 76ers 120-111 to close in on playoff spot|work=ESPN.com|date=10 April 2017|access-date=10 April 2017}} During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments to the [[Delaware Blue Coats|Delaware 87ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=5 December 2016}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2018–2019)=== On 25 July 2018, Luwawu-Cabarrot was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in a three-team deal involving the 76ers and the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/acquisitions-180725|title=Thunder Acquires Dennis Schröder and Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot|work=NBA.com|date=25 July 2018|access-date=25 July 2018}} ===Chicago Bulls (2019)=== On 1 February 2019, Luwawu-Cabarrot was traded with cash considerations to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for a protected 2020 second-round draft pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-finalize-trade-thunder|title=Bulls finalize trade with Thunder|date=1 February 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=1 February 2019}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2019–2021)=== On 30 September 2019, Luwawu-Cabarrot joined the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for training camp and played two preseason games before being waived.{{cite web|title=View 2019 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/training-camp-roster-2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=30 September 2019|date=30 September 2019}}{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Waive Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cavs-waive-four-players-191015|website=NBA.com|access-date=16 October 2019|date=15 October 2019}} On 23 October 2019, Luwawu-Cabarrot signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2019/10/23/brooklyn-nets-sign-timothe-luwawu-cabarrot-two-way-contract |website=NBA.com |access-date=23 October 2019 |date=23 October 2019}} On 15 January 2020, the Nets announced that they had signed Luwawu-Cabarrot to a 10-day contract.{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot to 10-day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/01/15/brooklyn-nets-sign-timoth-luwawu-cabarrot-to-10-day-contract |website=NBA.com |access-date=13 February 2020 |date=15 January 2020}} On 25 January, he was signed to a second 10-day contract.{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot to Second 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/01/25/brooklyn-nets-sign-timoth-luwawu-cabarrot-to-second-10-day-contract |website=NBA.com |access-date=13 February 2020 |date=25 January 2020}} On 7 February, Luwawu-Cabarrot signed a multi-year contract with the Nets.{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot to a Multi-Year Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/02/07/brooklyn-nets-sign-timothe-luwawu-cabarrot-multi-year-contract |website=NBA.com |access-date=13 February 2020 |date=7 February 2020}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2021–2022)=== On 22 September 2021, Luwawu-Cabarrot signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Johnny Hamilton, A.J. Lawson, Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot and Jahlil Okafor |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-johnny-hamilton-aj-lawson-timothe-luwawu-cabarrot-and-jahlil-okafor |website=NBA.com |access-date=22 September 2021 |date=22 September 2021}} On 24 September 2022, Luwawu-Cabarrot signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web |last=Weiner |first=Alex |title=Phoenix Suns sign Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot, Frank Jackson |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/3309403/phoenix-suns-sign-timothe-luwawu-cabarrot-frank-jackson |website=ArizonaSports.com |access-date=28 September 2022 |date =24 September 2022}} After appearing in three preseason games, Luwawu-Cabarrot was waived on 15 October.{{Cite web |title=Suns Waive Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot, Adonis Arms |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/10/suns-waive-timothe-luwawu-cabarrot-adonis-arms.html |access-date=2022-10-16 |website=Hoops Rumors |date=15 October 2022 |language=en-US}} ===Olimpia Milano (2022–2023)=== On 19 November 2022, Luwawu-Cabarrot made his return to Europe, signing with Italian and [[EuroLeague]] powerhouse [[Olimpia Milano]] in order to replace the injured [[Shavon Shields]].{{Cite web|title=Milan signs experienced forward Luwawu-Cabarrot|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/milan-signs-experienced-forward-luwawu-cabarrot/|website=[[EuroLeague]]|date=19 November 2022|accessdate=3 May 2024}} On 14 April 2023, he parted ways with the Italian club after the [[EuroLeague]] regular season had concluded. Luwawu-Cabarrot averaged 9.4 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.1 assists per contest in the [[EuroLeague]], as well as 11.9 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.6 assists in domestic league competition. ===ASVEL (2023–2024)=== On 3 August 2023, Luwawu-Cabarrot returned to his native France, signing a one-year deal with [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]] of the [[LNB Élite]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|url=https://ldlcasvel.com/la-bombe-tlc/|title=La bombe TLC!|last=|first=|date=August 3, 2023|website=ldlcasvel.com|publisher=|language=fr|access-date=August 4, 2023}} ===Baskonia (2024–2026)=== On 12 June 2024, Luwawu-Cabarrot signed a two-season contract with [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |first=Igor |last=Petrinovic |title=Baskonia completes Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot signing |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/baskonia-announces-luwawu-cabarrot/ |website=[[EuroLeague]] |date=12 June 2024 |accessdate=3 July 2026}} In his second season with Baskonia, Luwawu-Cabarrot led the [[2025–26 ACB season|2025–26 ACB]] in points with 18.1 [[points per game]] and made the [[All-Liga ACB Team|All-Liga ACB First Team]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.baskonia.com/es/noticias/timothe-luwawu-cabarrot-maximo-anotador-endesa-y-elegido-en-el-mejor-quinteto-de-acb|title=Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot, máximo anotador Endesa y elegido en el Mejor Quinteto de ACB|date=June 1, 2026|website=baskonia.com|publisher=|language=es|access-date=July 3, 2026}} He also helped the Basques win the [[2026 Copa del Rey de Baloncesto|2026 Copa del Rey]].{{Cite web |title=Baskonia stuns Real Madrid to lift Spanish Copa del Rey |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/baskonia-stuns-real-madrid-to-lift-spanish-copa-del-rey/ |website=[[EuroLeague]] |date=22 February 2026 |accessdate=3 July 2026}} ===Real Madrid (2026–present)=== On 17 July 2026, Luwawu-Cabarrot signed a two-year contract with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/timothe-luwawu-cabarrot-swaps-baskonia-for-real-madrid/|title=Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot swaps Baskonia for Real Madrid|date=July 17, 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|access-date=July 17, 2026}} ==National team career== Luwawu-Cabarrot played for the junior French national basketball teams in both the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], and the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]]. In 2015, he helped France to a semifinals appearance, while averaging 11.6 points and 4.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_UIfgjyQcGqk-fPlnl66Tj0.season_2014.roundID_10029.teamID_282.playerID_107611.html|title=TIMOTHE LUWAWU|work=FIBAEurope.com|access-date=3 July 2016}} Luwawu-Cabarrot was a member of the French national basketball team that finished second in the [[2020 Tokyo Olympics]]. In the gold medal match versus the [[United States men's basketball team]], Luwawu-Cabarrot scored 11 points in the losing effort, earning a silver medal. .{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-olympics-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401347899|title=ESPN|work=ESPN.com|access-date=7 August 2021}} ==Personal life== Luwawu-Cabarrot was born in France, and is of Congolese descent through his father.{{cite web | title=Luwawu-Cabarrot set for NBA Africa game, but savoring off-court experience | website=Oklahoman.com | date=3 August 2018 | url=https://oklahoman.com/article/5603717/luwawu-cabarrot-set-for-nba-africa-game-but-savoring-off-court-experience/ | access-date=18 August 2020}} ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player statistics
